findings.summary: An SSH prompt can still stall go
findings.evidence: GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 only stops git's HTTPS credential prompt. An SSH origin ([email]:...) that parse_remote accepts can still stall on an ssh passphrase or host-key prompt during ls-remote or push inside go. Fix: Also set GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -o BatchMode=yes' (or append BatchMode to an existing value) on the early step's git calls, or list SSH prompts as a known limit.
findings.location: Plan decision 5 / Risks: 'Early network calls ... hang go'

findings.summary: No seam named yet for the verifier/check ordering event
findings.evidence: The checks at run.rs:1684-1706 run through SnapExec over real commands, not through an injected fake. The plan lists the go-level scaffolding as an open question, so it has not confirmed that a 'scripted verifier/check fake' can write to the shared event log. Fix: Name the seam for the ordering point before coding: for example, a check command in the test config that appends to the log file, or the faked verifier agent invocation. Assert early push/open_pr happen before that event.

findings.summary: No test lands after a failed early push
findings.evidence: The criterion says 'land proceeds as today'. The go-level runs end at the verdict, and only criterion 3's second case covers land after a failed early open_pr. No test lands after a failed early push (no marker, nothing on the remote). Fix: Add a gh.rs case: early_push with a failing Remote::push, then land_pr. Assert it goes through publish exactly as with no early step: one push, one open_pr, merge_heads == [L].

findings.summary: The early PR body stays a placeholder forever
findings.evidence: Land builds the PR body from verification.summary (gh.rs:2133-2137). That does not exist at verification start, and land never rewrites the body. So every early-opened PR keeps a placeholder body, which changes what reviewers see. Fix: Use the same title as job.title(). Make the early body state that verification is in progress, and say in the change description that land does not refresh it. Or add a body update in land if PrHost already supports one.

findings.summary: PRs now open even for users who land without PRs
findings.evidence: Every non-nested go on a GitHub origin now opens a PR, including for users who never run the PR landing path. Fix: Mention in the CHANGELOG entry that any go on a GitHub origin opens a PR for the job's branch.

summary: I read gh.rs (land_pr, publish, refusal_text, parse_remote, Athena::land_pr), pr.rs (check_push, check_replace, PushRefusal) and run.rs (produce_and_verify, admission, verifier snapshot). The plan matches the code. Admission ends at run.rs:1640 and the verifier snapshot starts at :1645, so the insertion point is real and the nested guard has a model at :1669. land_pr reads remote_head at gh.rs:1789 and refuses when head != commit at :1797, so replace_early_head belongs there and in publish (:1956, check_push). check_replace ignores the ancestry answer, so gating it on the marker is the right fix for the foreign-head concern. parse_remote rejects non-GitHub URLs, so the silent skip can be decided inside GhEarly. Each demonstration fails without its behavior: the ordering and count assertions for criterion 1, the three-way outcome comparison for criterion 2, and the refusal you would get without the replace for criterion 3. Every finding is minor: PR body and scope, SSH prompts, a go-level ordering seam not yet confirmed, and how much of criterion 2's "land proceeds" is covered.
